title: Cancelling a Hotel Rate Plans Reservation: Who Acts, What Is Withheld
content:
Cancellation of a confirmed Hotel Rate Plans reservation rests on the clauses below. Three of them have been withdrawn and are marked as such; the rest are the basis the desk applies.

**1. Whose act it is.** Only the guest may cancel their own confirmed reservation, and the cancellation is confirmed by the guest rather than performed on their behalf.

**2. Which rooms.** The guest states in this conversation which of the rooms on the reservation they are giving up. What the guest says in the conversation is the authority for which rooms those are; the reservation record supplies how many rooms it holds and which reservation is meant.

**3. The free-cancellation term.** A cancellation is handled free of penalty only when frozen time is not after the moment the guest's reservation was confirmed by the property plus the free-cancellation term of the rate plan booked. The clock starts at the confirmation moment recorded on the reservation, which is a system record and not a matter of recollection. The free-cancellation term is counted in whole elapsed hours from the confirmation moment, never mixing elapsed hours with calendar days, and a cancellation confirmed exactly at the boundary is still free.

> **Withdrawn.** *"Inside the free-cancellation term nothing is withheld on any rate plan, and the deposit or prepayment is returned in full"* — this clause is **no longer in force**. It has been superseded by the current basis on which the withheld share is settled.

> **Withdrawn.** *"Outside it the penalty is read off the rate plan's cancellation ladder by how many whole days lie between the cancellation and the arrival date"* — this clause is **no longer in force** and has likewise been superseded.

**4. Where the ladder is silent.** Where the ladder is silent the plan's flat share of the room total applies, and where the plan expresses its penalty in room nights those nights are taken at the booked rate.

**5. A plan that returns nothing.** A plan that returns nothing withholds the whole room total and returns only the taxes the property itself does not keep.

**6. Giving up some rooms only.** A cancellation of some but not all rooms is penalised room by room on the rooms given up, and the remaining rooms keep their original terms.

> **Withdrawn.** *"The agency service fee is not returned on cancellation, because the booking service it pays for has already been performed."* — this clause is **no longer in force** and has been superseded on the question of whether that fee comes back.

## The free-cancellation term at its boundary

Counting runs in whole elapsed hours from the confirmation moment, and the two are never mixed with calendar days.

| Whole elapsed hours since the property confirmed | Plan's free-cancellation term | Handled free of penalty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fewer than the term | the term | yes |
| exactly the term | the term | yes, the boundary itself satisfying it |
| more than the term | the term | no |

A plan whose free-cancellation term is 0 hours admits no elapsed hours at all, so only a cancellation at the confirmation moment itself is not after it.

superseded_clauses: Inside the free-cancellation term nothing is withheld on any rate plan, and the deposit or prepayment is returned in full
Outside it the penalty is read off the rate plan's cancellation ladder by how many whole days lie between the cancellation and the arrival date
The agency service fee is not returned on cancellation, because the booking service it pays for has already been performed.
